title: Your First Hour
tagline: Follow the Academy route from your first training session to your first trip beyond the village.
blurb: Getting through the Academy, choosing your first stats, equipping starter gear, and finding your next objective.
heroAlt: A lantern-lit shinobi field desk overlooking a mountain road at dawn.
quickTake: Follow the Academy checklist in order; each step introduces a screen you will use later.
For the Academy route, equip four usable jutsu and both starter items.
The Resonance Trial is a practice spar. If you lose, adjust your loadout and try again; you will not be sent to the Hospital.

blocks.text: Choose your village for its setting and characters. It becomes your home and determines your village story, without a direct stat bonus. Transfers open at level 100 after you finish that story. The opening also introduces your companion and the Academy route.
Follow the short coach prompts as you learn each screen. You can keep playing while stat training runs; you do not need to wait for it before taking the next lesson.

blocks.label: Finding the next step
blocks.text: Open the Logbook when you lose track of your goal. It shows your current objectives and where to continue.

items: Start a stat-training session. The recommended stat and 15-minute timer are a useful first choice.
Unlock one extra jutsu for free in the Training Hall.
Equip at least four usable jutsu on your Profile.
Spend your 20 starting stat points and any Academy bonus points while you are on the Profile screen.
Equip both the Rustfang Kunai and Shinobi Vest.
Win the Academy's Resonance Trial with its turn-by-turn coaching.
Recover in the Noodle Den if you need to.
Claim the Academy Trial in the Mission Hall.
Open the Logbook and read the field assignment.
Travel to a numbered sector, inspect the Hollow Gate trace, then return to the village and complete the Field Seal ceremony.

blocks.text: Starting your first Academy training session brings you to level 2. From that level, the Awakening Stone in the Central Hub offers your first free random element. Completing the Academy brings you to at least level 10; the Field Seal is a keepsake, and Genin rank still begins at level 15.

Your first field assignments continue in order: win the E-Rank Drill and collect its reward, explore one field tile in a numbered sector, then visit the Pet Yard and use Pet or give an owned treat. Follow the field journal between steps. Afterward, the Logbook and Story Hall give you longer goals.

Start with the discipline used by the jutsu you enjoy. Its general stats help both attack and defense: Ninjutsu uses Willpower and Speed; Genjutsu uses Intelligence and Willpower; Taijutsu uses Strength and Speed; Bukijutsu uses Intelligence and Strength. The Training Plan recommends a stat for your current kit. Matching Offense and Defense stats support that same discipline.
Ninjutsu and Genjutsu spend Chakra. Taijutsu and Bukijutsu spend Stamina. Keep an affordable attack ready so one expensive sequence does not use up all your options.

blocks.label: Cover two ranges
blocks.text: For the Academy, carry something you can use up close and something that reaches a more distant target. Four equipped jutsu complete this lesson; your normal loadout can hold more.

sections.heading: When the first plan goes wrong

blocks.text: If a jutsu is greyed out, read its card. You may be short on AP, Chakra, or Stamina, outside its range, waiting on a cooldown, or missing a valid target. The spar coach walks you through Basic Attack, a ready jutsu, and Wait.

A spar never sends you to the Hospital. When another fight does, free checkout opens after the admission timer, normally 60 seconds. Discharge restores HP; use rest or the Noodle Den for Chakra and Stamina. Before trying again, change the part of your plan that failed.

blocks.label: Finish the return trip
blocks.text: Travel takes real time. At the field trace, finish the scene with Return with the evidence before heading home. Then accept the Field Seal and finish the return ceremony.

title: Levels, Ranks, and Daily Progress
tagline: Levels follow the stat points you earn through training, fights, and field work.
blurb: Levels and exam holds, stat training, jutsu lessons, daily work, and the Legacy path that opens at level 50.
heroAlt: A mission hall lined with maps, ledgers, and hanging lanterns.
quickTake: Level is derived from the stat points you have earned, so training is progression.
The 15-minute timer earns the most base stat gain per hour; longer timers need less attention.
Advancement pauses at levels 20 and 39 until you pass the required exam. Later ceremonies are optional.

blocks.text: Your level comes from the stat points you earn, including unspent points. Spend them on your Profile to shape your build.

blocks.caption: Rank unlocks, exam holds, and combat limits
head: Level
Rank
What changes
rows: First Awakening at 2; profession at 13; each stat capped at 350
Exam hold at 20; each stat capped at 700
Exam hold at 39; each stat capped at 1,300
Legacy offers become possible; each stat capped at 2,100

blocks.text: Genin and Chunin ranks arrive at levels 15 and 30. Your level cannot rise past 20 until you pass the Genin Advancement Exam, or past 39 until you pass the Chunin Advancement Exam. Check the Logbook for exam requirements. Jonin and Special Jonin arrive automatically at levels 50 and 80; their ceremonies are optional.

Choose a stat, compare the shown gain and Stamina cost, then start a timer. Training continues while you play or log out. At level 1 the rookie boost is six times the base gain, then it tapers down through level 35. Village and other bonuses can raise the amount shown.

blocks.caption: Base stat gain before the rookie boost and other bonuses
head: Session
Base gain
Stamina cost
Best for

blocks.text: Collect when the timer finishes, then start another session. Leaving a finished timer alone earns nothing extra. Short sessions have the best base hourly rate, but choose one you can realistically collect.

Points that would exceed the selected stat’s rank cap go into your unspent pool. Spend them on your Profile. Cancelling a running session keeps the progress earned so far, rounded down to whole points; the Stamina spent is not refunded.

blocks.alt: The Mission Hall interior where daily missions and the Academy Trial are claimed.
blocks.caption: Start at the Mission Hall, choose work that fits the time you have, and plan the rest of the session from there.

items: Collect finished training and start the next timer.
Complete up to 20 missions each UTC day. Choose work you can clear reliably.
Use the Hunting tab at the Shinobi Outpost for combat materials. You begin with 20 hunts per day, and each Hunter Rank adds one more, up to 25.
Look at Posted Contracts if you are already traveling; six rotate each UTC day.
Check your recovery and equipment before a boss fight or PvP queue.

blocks.text: Once-per-day field jobs and hunt claims also award unspent stat points. Pick the rewards you need now; you do not have to empty every daily counter.

Unlock an unlearned, eligible jutsu for free at mastery 1 in the Jutsu Training Hall. Further ryo lessons raise it one level at a time through mastery 30, within your rank cap. Base lessons take 10 minutes below mastery 10 and 30 minutes from there; the Hall shows the time and cost before you pay.

From mastery 30 to 40, lessons cost Honor Seals and use the same active lesson and queue slot. Mastery 41–50 is earned through PvP battles once your rank allows it. Ryo or Honor Seals can shorten a running lesson; compare the displayed price with how long remains.

Queue one paid lesson behind the current one. It starts when the first lesson finishes. Removing it before it starts gives a full refund. Cancelling the current lesson loses its progress, returns half its tuition, and fully refunds the queued lesson.

blocks.caption: Maximum jutsu mastery used in combat
head: Rank
Rank limit

blocks.text: Mastery matters most on the techniques you actually use. Work on a dependable attack and the supporting jutsu that keep you alive long enough to use it.

At level 50, the Wandering Sage may offer you a Legacy based on the way you have played. Keep taking missions, fighting, and exploring. Your Profile’s Legacy tab shows whether an offer is waiting and where to find him. Read each offered path’s trial activities and signature preview before choosing.

Accepting a Legacy is permanent. You can decline an offer and meet the Sage again later. Once you accept, trials take that same path through Awakened, Bound, Proven, and Mythic stages. Objectives count new progress from the trial’s start. Asking for a different proof changes the tasks and resets the current trial’s progress.

Bound, Stage III, grants your Legacy’s signature technique in an extra combat slot. Its mastery rises with the Legacy stage instead of through ordinary lessons. The Hall of Legends also records world Eras and offers longer personal campaigns; see Endgame Modes and How to Prepare before starting one.

title: Combat Fundamentals: Turns, Range, and Resources
tagline: Plan your move and attack together so you do not run out of AP in the wrong place.
blurb: Planning AP, reading range and targets, handling resource costs and status timing, and getting started in multiplayer combat.
heroAlt: Two shinobi measuring distance across a rain-dark citadel arena.
quickTake: You normally have 100 Action Points each turn. Review action costs before moving.
Control the distance so your opponent must spend AP reaching their preferred range.
Carry a reliable attack, a second range option, and one defensive or cleansing answer.

sections.heading: Plan the turn before you move

blocks.text: Before moving, check the distance, obstacles, and active ground zones. Then look at your AP, Chakra, Stamina, and cooldowns. Target highlights show what a selected action can reach.

A normal turn starts with 100 AP. Stun reduces that turn to 60 AP. Moving, weapon attacks, jutsu, and basic support actions spend from the same allowance. Status effects can change costs, so use the amount on the action card. Custom Bloodline techniques start at 40 AP for utility or 60 AP for damage.

blocks.label: If an action is greyed out
blocks.text: Check AP, range, cooldown, Chakra or Stamina, and valid targets. Moving closer only helps if you still have enough AP to act afterward.

Ninjutsu and Genjutsu use Chakra; Taijutsu and Bukijutsu use Stamina. Techniques marked Any use your specialty’s resource pool. Both pools grow with level and recover at the start of your turns. Costs also rise with level, so judge your plan by the current numbers on the cards.
When you want to close
Keep enough AP to attack when you arrive. If you cannot reach and attack in the same turn, stop where the opponent must spend AP to approach you.
When you want to kite

Attack before retreating when the position allows it. Keep a second ranged option ready for turns when your strongest one is on cooldown. Check the weapon in your hand as well; it has its own range and cooldown.
Terrain and weather can favor particular disciplines or elements. Read the battle’s terrain information and account for any ground zones before deciding where to stand.

Decide what the turn needs. You might pressure an opponent into defending, set up a later hit, recover from a bad exchange, or finish a weakened target. Spend your AP on that goal before adding another action.
Use Wait once you are done. A turn spent holding a safe position can let resources and cooldowns recover. Count what the opponent can reach before ending there.

blocks.label: Common mistake
blocks.text: Do not spend your last AP stepping into an opponent’s best range. You may be handing them an attack before you can use your own.

Cleanse removes your negative statuses, including ones waiting to activate. Clear removes an opponent’s active positive effects and breaks their shield, if they are in range. Both have a base cost of 60 AP and their own cooldowns. Check for Cleanse Prevent or Clear Prevent before spending the action.

Wound and Drain tick at the end of the affected fighter’s turn in Solo/PvP, or at round end in Towers. Cleanse can remove them before they tick. Poison also hurts you when you spend Chakra or Stamina on jutsu. If you are poisoned, compare the value of another cast with the damage it will cause you.
Use a shield before the heavy hit arrives. Movement is useful when it changes who can reach you or moves you out of a dangerous zone. Keep these options available alongside your damage jutsu.

AI practice and direct player spars in the Battle Arena do not affect ranked rating, and losing one never sends you to the Hospital. Team Arena is a four-player 2v2 mode with balanced teams, no consumables, and no rating, currency, or progression rewards. Queue solo and matchmaking finds the other three fighters.

Ranked 1v1 has its own ladder. For ranked 2v2, invite a partner who must accept; each player keeps a separate 2v2 rating, and matchmaking uses the pair’s average. Agree on a target before the fight and pay attention to the turn order before committing support actions.
Scheduled tournaments

Open Tournaments from the Arena District and read the format before signing up. Standard uses your own build, Ranked and 2v2 use Ranked Format, and pet events use one or two companions per owner. Your loadout locks at signup. A 2v2 partner must accept before signup closes.

Stay on the board and ready up each round; missing a deadline can eliminate you. The bracket is single elimination. Tournament rounds spend no consumables, change no ladder rating, and award no normal combat payout. The board records the champion.

blocks.label: Check before queuing
blocks.text: Check the Arena District for each mode’s current availability and entry rules.

title: Building a Loadout That Holds Up
tagline: Build a useful rotation, then add answers for the fights that give you trouble.
blurb: Loadout capacity, mastery, elemental Awakening, forged Bloodlines, gear upgrades, weapon attunement, and named equipment.
heroAlt: A dark cedar forge filled with tools, steel, and a restrained blue flame.
quickTake: You can equip 12 jutsu, or 15 with Shinobi Supporter. Start with a small rotation you know how to use.
Free elemental Awakenings unlock at levels 2 and 20. Check your gear and jutsu requirements before a paid reroll.
Use Bloodline Awakening’s point breakdown to fit the techniques you want within the ritual’s budget.

blocks.text: Your regular loadout holds 12 jutsu, or 15 with an active Shinobi Supporter membership. The Academy only asks for four. Start with a few techniques you can use together, then fill the remaining space with answers to particular problems.

items: Keep an affordable attack for ordinary turns.
Cover the range where that attack struggles.
Bring defense or movement for a bad position.
Choose a stronger hit that benefits from your other techniques.

blocks.text: Train mastery on the jutsu you cast regularly. On your Profile, check that each intended technique is learned, equipped, and usable with your current elements and Bloodline. Changing a Bloodline can change which techniques are available.
A Bound Legacy adds a separate signature slot at Stage III. The signature arrives at mastery 30, rises to 40 at Stage IV and 50 at Stage V, and does not need ordinary jutsu lessons.

Claim a free random element roll at the Awakening Stone at levels 2 and 20. A paid roll costs 10 Fate Shards for your primary element, keeping the secondary if you have one, or 15 to reroll both. You cannot choose the result. Check equipped gear and jutsu before replacing an element they need.

blocks.caption: Forged Bloodline ranks at the Central Hub Awakening Stone
head: Rank
Jutsu
Build points
Forge cost

blocks.text: Choose the rank whose budget fits the techniques you want to make. A higher rank allows more points, but each technique still needs a clear use in combat.

sections.heading: What makes a technique cost more

blocks.text: Custom techniques start as 40 AP utility or 60 AP damage. Range, targeting shape, cooldown, damage type, and effect tags can add build points. Read the itemized breakdown after each change; several small choices can put the whole Bloodline over budget.

Adjustable percentage effects offer 25% or 30% on B- and A-rank Bloodlines, and 30% or 35% on S-rank Bloodlines. Other effects have fixed magnitudes. Pierce scales with offense and mastery up to a damage cap and bypasses defenses. Read each effect’s description instead of assuming every percentage or tag works the same way.

blocks.label: Check the core idea
blocks.text: Before adding another effect, picture the turn when you would cast this technique. Keep the effects that make that turn work.

Use the Shop and Grand Marketplace for catalog purchases, and the Crafter for recipes. Direct player transfers send currency, not items. Sunscar Exchange handles eligible player listings. Check level and element requirements before spending materials or ryo.

Choose gear for the problem you are having in fights. Defense helps if you fall before your setup works. A weapon with suitable reach gives you another action when your jutsu are unavailable. Bring consumables allowed by the mode you are entering.
Relic equipment

Relics have their own equipment slot and improve damage against AI enemies. Some help all attacks; others favor an element or discipline. Their bonuses do not apply against players. Find them through village stories, biome chests, eligible Tower clears, ranked player wins, war crates, or the Weekly Boss. Check the level requirement and choose a bonus that fits your attacks. A duplicate relic awards 15 Fate Shards instead.
Upgrade gear

Some weapon and armor drops are improved versions of a catalog item. Each step adds 0.5 EP to a weapon or 0.5 percentage points of armor protection strength, staying below the next tier. Protection combines with other reductions with diminishing returns. Buying or crafting better gear unlocks drops from higher eligible upgrade tiers. Upgrade pieces cannot be bought or crafted, and spares sell for 500 ryo.
Upgrade drops can come from Ancient Chests and bosses at 5%, Clan Exchange caches at 1 in 5, and ordinary fights at 0.5%. Treat them as occasional finds while you work toward your next purchase.
Elemental weapon attunement

Hollow Gate bosses can drop Elemental Shards. Forge 10 into an Elemental Core at the Crafter, then use it from Inventory to attune a legendary or mythic melee weapon to an element you have awakened. Each attunement, including a change to another element, spends one Core. You must still have the weapon’s element to equip it.
Named equipment

At level 90, you can forge named weapons and armor. Name your piece first, then roll. Every roll costs 200 Fate Shards plus apex materials: Pristine Iron Sand, Legendary Material, an Ancient Beast Core, a Titan Bone for a weapon or Shadow Pelts for armor, Superior elemental minerals, and one relic. The price is paid when you roll, and every roll is yours to keep, so there is no discard or free re-roll. Named gear accepts Fate Shards only for its shard cost. The Crafter lists the full price and what you hold.
A named piece sells to the shop for 500 ryo. You can list an unworn piece at Sunscar Exchange, but equipping it once permanently removes that option. Decide whether to keep it before putting it on.

blocks.label: Before spending materials
blocks.text: Check the recipe or upgrade screen first. Hunter rank-ups, Bloodline forging, Hollow Gate keys, and weapon attunement use different materials.

title: Travel, Exploration, and World Events
tagline: Find your way through the connected world, read the ground, and prepare for trouble on the road.
blurb: Walking, exploration, gathering, road encounters, contracts, changing weather, and shared world events.
heroAlt: A lone shinobi looking across connected mountain roads, villages, and a distant storm.
quickTake: The map has 66 ordinary sectors plus special destinations. Follow connected roads and learn the places you use most.
Explore, Fishing, and Mining share 100 actions per UTC day. A sector's shared exploration pool is a separate limit.
The world completes a day every two real hours. Night work follows that clock, while daily allowances reset at midnight UTC.

sections.heading: Find your way on the map

blocks.alt: The world map showing villages, connecting roads, regions, and sector destinations.
blocks.caption: Use the overview to choose a destination, then follow the roads through its connected sectors.

blocks.text: In a sector, hold WASD or the arrow keys to walk. You can also click or tap a destination, or drag to steer. Follow a road through an exit to reach the next sector. Select a building or landmark to open its activity.

The World Map overview helps you find contracts, village borders, and event locations. Read the selected sector's details before setting out. Some trips use a travel timer; you cannot be attacked during that timed transit. Walking around a sector does not give you the same protection.

Each sector has a shared daily gathering pool used by Explore, Fishing, and Mining. As players work it, the sector changes from Rich to Worked Over to Picked Clean Today. The owning village has a larger allowance there, but the ground is still shared. If it is picked clean for you, follow the suggested roads to another sector or return after midnight UTC.

Your personal allowance is 100 actions per UTC day across Explore, Fishing, and Mining. Check the remaining count before committing to a contract or gathering trip. Moving to a fresh sector only helps while you still have personal actions left.

Explore can reveal a material find. Choose Field Herb, Binding Fiber, or Iron Sand. A regional trace lets you take two of that common material and one trace instead of three common materials. The preview shows the result before collection, and closing the find saves it for later.

sections.heading: Stop at fishing and mining sites

blocks.text: Look for shoal and mineral markers in the sector. Select one to see its skill requirement and remaining attempts, then use Approach to walk to the shore or rock base. Equip the right tool before starting: a fishing kunai for Fishing or a pickaxe for Mining.

Each ordinary site gives you three attempts, then replenishes after ten minutes. You can play the minigame for a success bonus or choose the relaxed animation at the baseline chance. Both spend an action, and failed or abandoned attempts still count. The Shinobi Outpost in Central lists known sites, tracks both skills, and lets you manage tools.

Travelers can offer supplies, healing, deliveries, trails, or a conversation. Some encounters lead to a choice or a fight. Recent player duels can also leave scars on the ground for up to 24 hours. Check the person or sign you have found before spending an action.

Road bandits offer Fight or Pay 500 ryo. Paying uses carried ryo and costs no HP. Other hostile road encounters offer Fight or Flee. Fleeing costs half your current HP, rounded down without knocking you out, and 10% of carried ryo up to the discharge cost for your level. Neither option takes banked ryo. The encounter shows the price before you choose.

sections.heading: Plan around contracts and the sky

blocks.text: Six sector contracts are posted each UTC day. They ask for 8 to 12 successful explores in the named sector, sometimes at night. Collect the reward from the contract when it is ready. Night-only progress must be earned at night, but you can collect a completed contract in daylight before the daily board changes.

A world day lasts two real hours, including about 45 minutes of night. Use the map's sky and contract status to tell whether night work counts now. This cycle does not reset your daily actions or contracts; those still use midnight UTC.

Scheduled weather can change every 40 real minutes and may hold for several windows. Check the forecast and current combat modifier before fighting. A clan that holds a sector can set local weather there.

blocks.label: Sunscar Festival
blocks.text: The sun icon opens Sunscar Festival. Sector 54 is its entrance rather than an ordinary travel area. Check the festival's own rules before entering an event or placing a wager.

sections.heading: Join a roaming World Boss event

blocks.text: Open World Bosses to check the active threat, its current sector, and the event clock. Travel to the boss's sector and join the public queue. A squad launches with three players, or with one or two when the 30-second queue timer ends. Recover before joining: you enter with your current HP and keep the HP remaining afterward. A knockout sends you to the Hospital.

Event crystal veins offer another way to help. Mine a Hollow Shard, then turn it in on the World Bosses screen for contribution points and progress toward weakening the boss. Turn shards in before the event ends. Only deposited shards help weaken the boss.

During its final stand, the boss stays in place until the event clock ends. If it survives, the threatened village receives 24 hours of Ashfall with 5% lower training gains and 5% longer jutsu lessons. Read the event screen for the current outcome and your recorded contribution.

sections.heading: Help your village answer a crisis

blocks.text: During the Fourfold Breach, each village fills its own defense target. The crisis ends when all four villages finish, and the leaderboard records the top contributors.

During Hollow Gate Reckoning, choose the shinobi front or bring a ready companion team to the companion front. Either front helps your village reach its target. Check your health, loadout, and available companions before committing an attempt.

When a Dojo Circuit is scheduled, join through your village and begin a trial before playing. Earn seals through shinobi sparring, Chronicle duels, and a rewarded Pet Colosseum win. Combat seals record automatically. Return to the Circuit to record AI card and companion wins before the event closes.

The pet trial keeps the Colosseum's normal cost and reward limit. Circuit rewards are recorded honours and a place in the event archive, with no extra currency or rating. Use the event board to check what you still need.

title: Clans, Village War & Shared Stores
tagline: Know which campaign you are joining and what your clan or village needs from you.
blurb: Clan Hall goals, campaign queues, Golden Shrines, five-day Village Wars, field orders, shared stores, and territory.
heroAlt: A village command hall with maps, supply ledgers, and a council table.
quickTake: Clan War has 24 hours of preparation followed by 72 hours of scoring. Village War has one hour of preparation followed by five days.
Clan campaign queues share daily limits. Golden Shrine bonus matches have their own allowance and require you to travel there.
Use the Clan Hall for clan goals and rations. Use Town Hall for village stores, war objectives, and field orders.

sections.heading: Start with the Clan Hall overview

blocks.text: Join a clan from your village, then check its overview and pinned notices. The overview points you toward the current campaign, Boss Operations, and mentorship. If you are unsure where to help, ask what the clan is working toward this week.

Weekly contracts reward scored clan-war matches and Boss assaults with active clanmates. Collect the clan reward once a contract is complete. Restore the Hall is a separate weekly project that consumes Field Herb, Binding Fiber, or Iron Sand. Each member can contribute up to ten materials toward its shared target of 40. Four completed projects earn the permanent Restored Hall decoration.

An assignment tells your clan how you plan to help. Your clan rank decides which controls you can use. Earned Clan Points buy personal rewards in the Exchange and share a 1,000-point weekly earning cap. Exchange shelves open at Clan Levels 1, 7, 15, 25, and 40. Check an item's purchase limit before saving toward it.

sections.heading: Prepare for a Clan War campaign

blocks.text: Leadership declares a campaign for 100 Honor Seals. Both clans must be at least seven days old and have four eligible members. An eligible member is level 15 or higher, joined at least 48 hours ago, and has played within seven days. The war roster is fixed at declaration, so joining a clan during preparation does not add you to that campaign.

After 24 hours of preparation, fighting runs for 72 hours. Enter a Shinobi Duel, Shinobi Team Battle, Pet Showdown, or Chronicle Showdown queue. A team battle needs two clanmates. When matched, every player has 30 seconds to confirm readiness; attempts are spent when everyone confirms.

blocks.caption: Normal Clan War limits and scoring
head: Rule
What it means
rows: A 1v1 uses one slot for your clan; a 2v2 uses two.
Five personal slots per war day
All four battle modes use the same personal allowance.
A solo victory earns 100; a 2v2 team victory earns 200.
The attempts remain spent. No victory points are added.

blocks.text: The higher score at the end wins, with equal scores drawing. Played battles award 25 Clan Points plus 25 for a win. If your clan wins, members who played a scored battle receive another 75 Clan Points and a Legendary War Crate. These points share the weekly earning cap. After a campaign, clans recover for three days, and the same rivals cannot declare again for seven days.

Leadership can authorize 30 clan rations for a war day to add 10% to match Clan Points. This is optional and does not raise War Points or battle limits. Check the war panel before donating rations for that purpose.

Six Golden Shrines appear during a clan campaign, each with a two-hour window. The war panel reveals its sector and battle mode before opening. Travel to that sector to enter the bonus queue. Shrines use shinobi duels, Pet Showdown, or Chronicle Showdown, with each specialty appearing twice.

Each appearance has five bonus matches shared by the two clans and two attempts per member. A victory earns 100 bonus War Points. This allowance is separate from normal daily slots. New matches stop 15 minutes before a shrine window or the campaign closes, so arrive early enough to finish.

The seated Kage declares Village War using village War Resources. One hour of preparation is followed by five full days of scoring. Town Hall shows the score, strongholds, shrine schedule, and field orders. The higher final score wins; equal scores draw. Village War results do not transfer sector ownership.

Wins against players from the enemy village count toward the war. Spars and ranked matches do not. Each village also has three strongholds, one for shinobi combat, one for pet battles, and one for cards. You can queue to defend your own stronghold from Town Hall while online and available. Attackers must travel to the enemy stronghold and enter it. Its appointed ANBU defends when no player is queued.

The War Shrine opens for five two-hour windows during the campaign. Use the displayed schedule, which shows your local opening and closing times. Travel to its sector and enter the shrine room to take part. For current declarations, the first ten shared shinobi victories in each window earn 20 extra points each. Normal role victory points and enemy score deductions continue after that cap.

The village with the most accumulated uncontested time inside receives the 100-point window bonus. Empty or contested time does not count, and a tie awards no bonus. Staying inside with allies can help hold control, but adding more players does not make the clock run faster.

sections.heading: Help with a village field order

blocks.text: Accept one field order at a time from Town Hall, then follow its instructions on the World Map. Orders earn supporting points and shared intelligence that reveals enemy strongholds. Supporting PvE points can provide up to 20% of the total war score, so they help a fighting village rather than replacing player battles.

blocks.caption: What each field order asks you to do
head: Order
Your task
rows: Collect the package at your village outskirts, then deliver it to the assigned allied depot. Stay still for the displayed pickup and delivery timers.
Hold three different eligible enemy sectors for 20 seconds each.
Enter the assigned enemy stronghold and defeat its sentry or an enemy player inside.

blocks.text: Each player has four attempts per campaign day, with at most one Supply, two Sabotage, and two Espionage attempts. ANBU fallback assaults share the Sabotage allowance. An attempt is spent when accepted, even if you abandon it or lose. Movement, travel, combat, or a lost connection resets an unfinished stationary hold. Check the order's reset timer instead of assuming it changes at midnight.

Village Provisions come from donated ration packs and packed village supplies. Cook rations in the Noodle Den; gathered ingredients and fish support its recipes. Donated crafting materials and relics become Materials. The Supply Depot converts Materials into War Resources and advanced structures also require them.

The daily UTC store update removes 5% of stored Provisions, then uses the remaining stock to supply sector wars, mercenaries, and garrisons. An unfed side receives reduced structure bonuses. Garrison feeding is a separate choice that changes how many supporting points assaults can bank. Check the war map's feeding status and Town Hall's donation limits before committing ingredients you still need.

Watchtower, Barracks, and War Academy preparations belong to an individual war and end with it. Leadership should check their current scouting, upkeep, or support effect before spending War Resources. Supply Depot and Treasury Vault upgrades are permanent.

Sector Wars decide village control of land. A clan can plant its banner only in a sector its village already controls. The clan needs at least ten members, no other held sector, and 75 Territory Control Scrolls in its treasury. Leadership spends all 75 together to capture; partial deposits do not reserve a claim.

Once a sector is held, check its HP and guard status. Reinforcement scrolls repair damage. A breached sector has a fixed repair deadline and stops producing rewards or bonuses until restored. Weather and terrain choices matter only while the hold is active.

The weekly Clan Boss has a health pool shared by your clan. Parties bring one to four players. Use the ready room to agree on roles and check loadouts before starting. Prepare any needed supplies in the Crafter.

Contribution includes damage, healing, shielding, cleanses, objectives, and survival. Weekly rewards use recorded contribution, so support work matters. Active contributors also have a 5% chance of a gear piece from each assault. If saving the result fails, use Retry before leaving the operation.

title: Raise a Squad You Trust
tagline: Care for companions at Pet Home, then choose a team for Showdown, Warfront, ranked battles, or expeditions.
blurb: Carried companions, Sanctuary, wild binding, care, evolution, breeding, expeditions, and the different pet battle modes.
heroAlt: A shinobi handler preparing four distinct companion beasts in a lantern-lit sanctuary.
quickTake: Carry five companions, or six with supporter capacity. Sanctuary has no ownership cap and keeps extra companions safe.
Showdown lets you give orders each turn. Warfront tests the formation you set before each clash.
Ranked Pet Colosseum uses four carried companions in a player-controlled 2v2 battle with two reserves. Save their ranked loadouts before queuing.

sections.heading: Pet Home and your carried roster

blocks.text: Pet Home links to Collection, Pet Yard, Pet Arena, Sanctuary, and the Shinobi Hatchery. You can carry five companions by default, or six with supporter capacity. Set your Active companion in the Yard for shinobi fights and choose a 2v2 Partner where needed.

Sanctuary stores companions without an ownership cap. Captures and hatches go there automatically when your carried roster is full. Move a carried companion into Sanctuary to make room, then use Add to carried on the one you want to bring out.

blocks.label: Stored companions need a carried slot
blocks.text: A companion in Sanctuary cannot fight, train, breed, or leave on an expedition. Preserved overflow also needs a carried slot before it can take part. Releasing a companion ends that bond permanently.

Check happiness in the Yard before training or summoning a companion. It falls at daily resets. Petting has a daily allowance; treats and Bond training also help. A happy companion trains better, while low happiness can weaken its help in shinobi fights and make it disobey.

Choose a training focus and duration in Growth & training, then collect the result when it finishes. Only your active five carried companions can start training. If a supporter companion is outside that group, select it as Active or 2v2 Partner, or rest another companion in Sanctuary. Training continues during pet battles, but it must be collected before an expedition.

The five starter species have two evolutions. The first needs level 50 and an Awakening Stone; the second needs level 90 and an Ascension Stone. Check the evolution panel for the next form and the missing requirement. Other species do not currently evolve.

sections.heading: Binding wild pets and raising an egg

blocks.text: Wild binding uses a companion battle. Lower the wild pet's Resolve, then use a Beast Seal while it still has HP. Read its trait clue: some settle faster when you Rest or Guard, while others respond to landed attacks. A defeated pet cannot be bound.

Each seal shows how low Resolve must be before you can use it. Stronger seals can be used earlier. Activating one spends it, even if the bind fails; a failed bind leaves the fight running. Watch both Resolve and HP so an extra attack does not cost you the capture.

The Hatchery accepts one pair at a time. Choose two different available carried companions of the same element, each at least level 50 with a breeding use remaining. Each attempt spends one use from each parent and has an 80% chance to produce an egg. A successful egg goes to Sanctuary and incubates for 12 hours of active gameplay; time pauses while the game is closed or in the background. The hatch animation starts automatically when incubation ends, after your current battle, event, or dialog finishes. The Hatchery shows the species odds before you commit. Species and Chromatic appearance remain a surprise until hatching; Chromatic odds are 0.05% per egg (1 in 2,000).

Training Grounds and the Colosseum offer 1v1, 2v2, and 3v3 Showdowns against AI, with up to two reserves. Pick moves, swaps, and targets each turn. These AI matches have no turn timer. Training Grounds is unlimited practice without rewards; the Colosseum matches an opponent to your team and pays wins up to its daily limit.

Rest restores stamina without healing. Overdraft lets a companion use a move it cannot afford, but costs HP and its next action. Switches happen before attacks, so a reserve can change a bad matchup. By round 25, any unfinished fight is judged by companions left, remaining HP, stamina, then speed.

items: Keep a reserve that can answer your lead's weak matchup.
Check stamina costs and preparation requirements before committing a heavy move or signature.
Use Guard or a partner's protection when another companion needs to Rest.
Breeding and active expeditions make companions unavailable. Training can continue while they fight.

blocks.text: Beastbound Warfront fields four companions at once in automatic formation combat. Bring exactly four available carried companions and place them in any four of the ten deployment cells. Two rival positions are scouted before you lock your formation. The first side to win two clashes wins the match; each clash is decided by companions standing, then remaining health.

Placement sets up the fight. Forward positions make contact sooner; rear positions give ranged and support companions more room. Cover, shoji, smoke, and line of sight affect the routes and targets they can use. Read the clash report and reposition any companion before the next clash.

blocks.label: Build around what the squad does
blocks.text: Defenders hold up under pressure, Trackers pressure from range, Assassins threaten vulnerable targets, and Sages support the group. Any role or element mix is allowed. Start with a formation you understand, then change the position that failed. Collect completed expeditions before entering Warfront.

Ranked Pet Colosseum is a live 2v2 battle with two reserves. Select four available carried companions, then choose your opening pair after reviewing the opposing squad. Both players give their own orders each round. Competitive stats are balanced at level 50; your companions keep their species, evolved forms, and training outside the match.

In the Yard's Battle & techniques section, equip four learnable techniques alongside the companion's permanent signature. Choose a preset or adjust its competitive attributes and item, then save the ranked loadout. The same choices appear in the ranked squad builder, where you can review them before queuing.

Lock orders for both active companions before the planning clock runs out. Rest and switching help manage stamina; repeated Guard becomes more expensive and less effective. Ranked results change Pet Elo. Unranked player-controlled rooms use the sparring roster and a room code. Neither mode spends ryo or battle items.

Scout unlocks at companion level 20 and takes 45 minutes. Forage unlocks at level 50 and takes two hours; Ruins unlocks at level 80 and takes four. Higher-level companions can still choose lower routes. Higher routes offer larger hauls and better ryo and pet XP per hour. Check the Board's preview for the selected pet and your profession.

Choose Safe or Bold and an optional provision before departure. Bold improves the haul but costs happiness on return; a provision is consumed when the pet leaves. When it returns, Secure haul keeps the listed rewards, while Investigate final lead risks a smaller haul for a chance at more. Daily start and collection limits are shown on the Board.

Every eligible companion earns ryo and materials, plus pet XP while it can still grow. All three routes bring a random assortment of hunting, fishing, mining, and harvesting materials: 3 for Scout, 6 for Forage, and 12 for Ruins before bonuses. Better-quality material rolls rise from 15% to 40% to 65%; harvesting uses its existing common and regional supplies. No gathering skill XP is awarded. Bone Charms can appear on any route, while Aura Stones are a rare Ruins find. Each route can also find 2–4 Fate Shards, with base chances of 3% for Scout, 6% for Forage, and 12% for Ruins; profession and find bonuses raise those chances. Pet Tamers receive 50% more expedition rewards and earn profession XP; purchased Expeditioner perks still apply. Collect the expedition to free that companion for its next assignment.

The Pet Gauntlet uses a separate draft of temporary companions. Recruit, place, and improve that squad during the run. Its companions do not join your owned collection, so you can try combinations without changing your carried roster.
Pet Rally at Sunscar Festival

Bring an available companion to race at Sunscar Festival. Practice is always open. Species sets its racing style, while trained stats give capped bonuses. Learn the turns, jumps, Burst, and elemental moves before entering the daily Grand Prix.

The Grand Prix has three races and one entry per UTC day, used when the first race begins. Finish all three for ryo and Rally reputation. Combined race time breaks points ties. If you leave partway through, resume the unfinished Grand Prix from the race desk.

title: Chronicle Showdown: Rules and Deck Basics
tagline: Build a legal deck, read the field, and choose packs that help your next upgrade.
blurb: Deck limits, turns, Tributes, Calls, Warded Monsters, Snares, elements, Chronicle Point packs, and practice modes.
heroAlt: A Shinobi Chronicle Showdown board with opposing fields and card zones.
quickTake: Bring exactly 40 cards, open with five, and protect 8,000 Health.
The first player skips the opening draw and cannot Battle that turn. Plan your opening around the field you leave behind.
Basic packs use Chronicle Points earned in Echoes of War. Choose an element, Jutsu, or Snares when your deck needs a particular kind of card.

blocks.text: Shinobi Chronicle Showdown is the card duel in the Card Hall. If the Hall is locked, reach level 17 and find the Chronicle Scribe on the world map for your first deck. The Hall's Collection, Deck Builder, and Packs sections let you read your cards, save a deck, and buy packs.

The Living Chronicle in the Story Hall keeps a broader record: story progress, Showdown and companion wins, missions, exploration, recent wars, clan contribution, and Legacy. You do not build a deck there.

blocks.alt: A Showdown board divided into player and opponent fields with clear summon, set, and battle areas.
blocks.caption: Both fields stay visible. Read the card text and target preview before committing a summon or attack.

sections.heading: Save a deck you can actually play

blocks.text: A legal deck has exactly 40 cards, using copies you own. Most cards allow three copies, but printed LIMIT 1 or LIMIT 2 rules take priority. Check Deck Builder's warnings and save the finished list before starting a duel.

Keep enough level 1 to 4 Monsters to establish a field without Tributes. A hand full of large Monsters can leave you unable to Summon. Add a smaller group of Tribute Monsters, then use Jutsu and Snares that support the same plan. Upgrade the starting deck a few slots at a time and test whether those cards help you play a stronger opening.

Read effects as well as ATK and DEF. FLIP effects reward setting up a face-down Monster, and some Snares need a matching face-up element. A powerful card that rarely meets its own requirements may fit another deck better.

The turn follows Draw, Standby, Main 1, Battle, Main 2, and End. Draw, Standby, and End resolve automatically. The player who takes the first turn skips that turn's draw and cannot enter Battle. You get one Normal Summon or Set across both Main phases. Skipping Battle also skips Main 2. Smart Phase Assist moves past completed attacks, while you still choose your plays.

Level 1 to 4 Monsters need no Tribute, level 5 to 6 need one, and level 7 to 8 need two. A Set Monster enters face-down Defense and may Flip Summon later. Shadow Clone creates two Shadow Doubles that can be Tributed from the next turn. They vanish when they leave the field and do not satisfy a Snare's elemental requirement.

Each Call Jutsu Summons its own matching Level 8 beast for 1,000 Health. You need that beast in hand, the Call uses your Normal Summon, and the beast cannot attack that turn. Called beasts cannot be Summoned another way. Other level 7 to 8 Monsters are Warded: Snares cannot destroy them or return them to the hand during the turn they are Summoned. Jutsu can still affect them.

Set Snares during a Main phase and wait a turn before using them. When the printed trigger occurs, you may use one matching response. Read its element requirement, targets, and Health cost before confirming. Target previews show the expected battle result, but a face-down card or response can change what happens.

blocks.label: Before entering Battle
blocks.text: Check your Normal Summon, your Monster positions, and any response you meant to Set. Direct attacks require an empty opposing Monster field. You lose at zero Health, when you must draw from an empty deck, or by forfeiting.

The wheel is Fire over Wind, Wind over Lightning, Lightning over Earth, Earth over Water, and Water over Fire. With no Field Jutsu active, advantage adds 200 to the ATK or DEF used in that battle. A Field Jutsu replaces the wheel: its favored element gains 300 ATK and the opposed element loses 200 ATK. Only one Field applies at a time.

Elemental variety can help with bad matchups, but it should still fit your deck. Check whether a Field also helps the opponent before playing it, and keep the face-up Monsters your Snares need to work.

Basic packs cost Chronicle Points earned through Echoes of War in the Celestial Tower. Each contains five Common or Rare cards. Random Packs can contain Monsters of any element, Jutsu, and Snares. Element packs contain only matching Monsters; Jutsu and Snare packs focus on those card types.

Premium packs cost Fate Shards. Elite gives one Rare or Epic card, Legendary gives one Legendary, and the two Quintet packs give five Epic or five Legendary cards. Read the listing for the current price and pool. Cards are equally likely within each pack's eligible pool, and duplicates can appear even within one pack. Owning a card does not lower its chance of appearing again.

Swipe across a pack or press Tear open, then tap through the cards. Skip goes straight to the summary, where you can tap any card to read it full size. The cards are already yours when the reveal begins, so skipping or closing it does not lose them. Open another buys another pack; if a purchase was interrupted, use the Recover button shown for that pack.

AI spar lets you test against Easy, Medium, or Hard. Free-play PvP lets you queue or challenge another player without risking rating. Neither awards ryo or rating. Start with Easy while you learn your opening, then try harder opponents as your deck improves.

AI wins update your Showdown record and can count toward Legacy. Free-play wins can count too when both players take part. Forfeits, timeouts, unfinished games, and very short matches do not qualify. Echoes of War supplies the Chronicle Points for Basic packs. Clan and Village War can also use Showdown results toward their own objectives.

title: Professions, Gathering, and Ryo
tagline: Choose work you enjoy, learn the field skills, and save materials for a purpose.
blurb: Profession ranks and Mastery, Fishing and Mining, gathering tools, material use, and everyday money decisions.
heroAlt: Three shinobi representing the Healer, Vanguard, and Pet Tamer professions.
quickTake: Professions unlock at level 13. Healer, Vanguard, and Pet Tamer each have a hub with daily work and rank progress.
Fishing and Mining are separate skills available alongside any profession. Start with a basic tool and a skill-1 site.
Bank spare ryo, collect interest when it is ready, and check a recipe before refining or donating its ingredients.

sections.heading: Choose the profession you will use

blocks.caption: The three profession paths
head: Profession
Typical work
Why choose it
rows: Treat wounded or knocked-out allies in the village ward
You enjoy helping players recover and supporting group fights.
Fight eligible real-player opponents and take part in wars
You want to earn Honor Seals through PvP.
Train companions, collect expeditions, and fight with pets
You want faster companion training and better PvE or expedition rewards.

blocks.text: Your first choice unlocks at level 13. Each profession advances through ten ranks. Profession XP earned after rank 10 becomes Mastery points, which you spend in that profession's Mastery panel. The Mastery panel shows each path's effects and the price of a reset.

From character level 20, you can change professions using a Profession Change Scroll. The Grand Marketplace sells it for 200 Fate Shards beside the Village Transfer Scroll. Each change starts the new profession at Rank 1 with 0 profession XP and no Mastery. Previous profession progress does not carry over.
Your profession hub tracks your rank and lists today's missions. Start there if you want profession XP but aren't sure what to do next.

Healers spend chakra to restore allies and earn XP from the share of HP restored. Vanguards earn Honor Seals from qualifying real-player kills, with daily and per-target limits shown in the hub. Pet Tamers improve pet PvE and training speed. Every expedition receives their fixed 50% reward bonus, with purchased Expeditioner perks adding further benefits.
Clan Boss actions can also award profession XP for useful work in the fight. Healing and other support actions count alongside damage, so choose a role your current loadout can perform.

Visit the Shinobi Outpost in Central for the Fishing and Mining tabs. These skills have their own XP and levels, separate from your profession. The Outpost lists sites and their requirements. Begin at a skill-1 site, then move to rich sites at skill 4 and master sites at skill 7.

Buy a Basic Fishing Kunai or Basic Pickaxe from the Ryo Shop and equip it in its gathering slot through Inventory or the Outpost. Each basic tool lasts 50 attempts. Golden tools in the Grand Marketplace never break. Gathering tools do not take a combat equipment slot or add battle stats.

On the World Map, select a shoal or mineral node and approach its marked shore or rock base. Lead moving fish and land a tethered Fishing Kunai, with three throws per attempt. Fish display their required Fishing level. Hitting one above your level fails the attempt; misses scatter the shoal. Mining uses Veinbreaking: place chakra paper seals along the faults, then release the fractures. Each pocket needs one fracture; crossing fractures crush the ore. The seals ignite in placement order. A clean fracture still uses your Mining skill's extraction chance. Watch animation uses your skill’s baseline success chance.

A success awards 10 skill XP and a resource. A completed failure awards 3 XP. Each ordinary node allows three attempts before a ten-minute refill. Explore, Fishing, and Mining share 100 total actions per UTC day. Starting spends the action and one basic-tool use, even if you fail or abandon the attempt.

sections.heading: Check a recipe before using materials

blocks.text: Better gathering skills improve success and resource quality, within the site's quality limit. Keep the grade a recipe asks for. Fine ore supports rare gear, Superior ore supports epic weapons, and Pristine ore supports legendary weapons. Regional minerals supply specialized recipes.

The Outpost's Mineral Refinery can turn one Fine, Superior, or Pristine mineral into two, three, or four common ingredient units. That conversion cannot be reversed. Check your next weapon recipe before breaking down a higher-grade stack.

Fish can be cooked into ration packs in the Noodle Den. The recipe also needs Field Herb, Heartwood Bark, and ryo. Higher-grade fish make more rations, within the 40-ration daily cooking allowance. Packed village supplies and donated rations help shared stores; common gathered materials can also fund your clan's Hall project.

Hunt materials still have separate uses in Hunter Rank, crafting, and pet treats. Before donating or converting a stack, check the recipe or rank-up you are saving for. Gather the missing ingredients for that goal instead of trying to fill every stack at once.

items: Carry enough ryo for your next purchase or recovery and bank what you can spare. Road fleeing can take carried ryo, but it does not touch the Bank.
Bank interest requires banked ryo and at least one Town Hall Bank upgrade. A new claim becomes available after each full 24-hour interval and must be collected manually.
Use the Shop and Grand Marketplace for catalog purchases. Compare the stats and effects with equipment you already own before spending.
Direct player transfers send currency, not items. They are permanent and taxed, and they do not protect a separate item trade.

blocks.text: Set aside the ryo and ingredients for your next upgrade, then donate what you can spare.

title: Endgame Modes and How to Prepare
tagline: Choose a challenge by its entry rules, the team it needs, and what you risk on a loss.
blurb: Prepare for Tower climbs, the Weekly Boss, Hollow Gate, Strongholds, and the longer campaigns.
heroAlt: A shinobi approaching monumental battle towers under a storm-lit sky.
quickTake: Check the lobby before entering. Battle Towers, Endless Tower, and Endless Spire have different party rules and loss penalties.
The Weekly Boss has unlimited health. Deal damage for the leaderboard during its 72-hour event; each player gets three attempts per spawn.
Resume an unfinished Hollow Gate run to keep using the entry you already paid for. A fresh standard run spends a key.

sections.heading: Battle Towers, Endless Tower, and Endless Spire

blocks.alt: The Battle Towers rising above a mountain settlement with a shinobi at the approach.
blocks.caption: Review the lobby before entering; the three Tower modes have different party rules, risks, and rewards.

blocks.text: Battle Towers

Battle Towers have fixed encounters with objectives, hazards, bosses, and first-clear rewards. Your first three entries into uncleared floors each UTC day are free; later entries cost 1,500 ryo. Replaying a cleared floor is free. Read the objective before choosing your squad.
Story Tower rooms hold two to four fighters. You can fill one slot with a reduced-strength AI helper, so a host and helper can launch a two-slot room. The helper earns no rewards.
Endless Tower

Each wave gets harder, and you carry your remaining HP into the next fight. Cash out between waves to keep your run earnings. Defeat costs the unclaimed ryo and sends you to the Hospital; milestone currencies stay yours. Your first fresh run each UTC day is free. Later starts cost 3,000 ryo more each time, while resuming an active run is free.
Endless Spire

Endless Spire is a 20-stage boss climb for exactly four players. It has weekly blessings, keystones, and a leaderboard. There are no AI helpers. Agree on who will handle the boss mechanics before the party starts.

The Weekly Boss is a damage challenge against an enemy with unlimited health. It stays available for its 72-hour event, regardless of total damage dealt. Track its current sector in the Weekly Boss view, then find it there to fight. You have three attempts per spawn, each costing 20 stamina.

Prepare before spending an attempt. You enter with your current HP, Chakra, and remaining Stamina, and the fight has a 20-round limit. Keep enough defense to survive while dealing damage across several turns.

Rewards arrive when the event ends. Every contributor earns a ryo share and a once-per-week grant of 10 stat points. The top 25 receive a Dungeon Key, and the top 10 also receive a Weekly Boss Core. Contributors can also receive an upgrade gear drop. Check the reward panel after the timer ends.

A relic dungeon has three seals: defeat the Warden with your shinobi, win the Chronicle match, then beat the Rare Beast with a companion. Bring an available companion and a usable Chronicle deck before entering.
Progress saves between seals. After the third win, choose Claim dungeon reward on the dungeon screen.

sections.heading: Hollow Gate entry, risk, and Attunement

blocks.text: A standard Hollow Gate dive is a five-floor expedition through a partly hidden map. Your village needs an active 30-day access seal opened by its seated Kage. A fresh standard run spends one Hollow Gate Key and one daily entry. The base allowance is two starts per UTC day, with an extra start available through Attunement. Resume an unfinished run instead of paying for a new one.

Choose one of the offered augments at the start. Its benefit and drawback apply to that run. Follow the map markers to descend, and decide whether optional chest detours are worth the extra steps. Shrine Keys found inside open doors; they are separate from the Hollow Gate Key used for entry.

Hollow Hounds can be fought by your shinobi. If you want to use a companion instead, bring an active, carried pet with PvE unlocked, normally at pet level 50. It must not be breeding or away on an expedition. Training can continue during the duel.

Extract to keep your haul. If you die or abandon the run, you keep 50% of the currencies you earned inside. Each Greedy Hands rank raises that share by 10 percentage points, up to 80%. Items and permanent progress stay yours. Spend Hollow Shards on permanent Attunement upgrades at the Shrine, choosing the ones that address what is ending your runs.

Wandering quest givers can send you to shorter Rifts, from one to three floors. These have their own level requirements and do not spend a Hollow Gate Key, but they share the Gate daily start allowance. Accept the quest and travel to its marked sector.

A weekly Rift signal marks an existing chest, encounter, or shard vein on each floor. It helps you choose a route. You can fight as a shinobi without bringing a pet, and card ambushes lend a starter deck if you do not have one. Defeat the named quest boss to receive the completion reward, then check the run summary before leaving.

Stronghold exploration opens at character level 50. Enter from the sector and watch your threat as you walk. At full threat, you must resolve a patrol fight before continuing. Leaving or reloading does not clear a patrol you already triggered.

The War Archives offer an optional intel objective. ANBU treasury raids are a separate level-100 activity: reach the vault inside a rival stronghold and clear any patrol before challenging its defender. Check the raid panel for the target, available rewards, and daily allowance before committing.
Open the Celestial Tower from the Central Hub to find its campaigns alongside the Tower climbs. Echoes of War is a Chronicle card campaign; its victories earn Chronicle Points for Basic packs.

The First Pact opens at character level 100. Bring four available carried companions for its two active positions and two reserves. Explore the Sunken Court, speak to its residents, and use the journal to follow your current objective. Later trials and Court work continue after the main story, so check the journal when an objective ends.

sections.heading: Era campaigns in the Hall of Legends

blocks.text: An unlocked world Era opens a personal campaign in the Hall of Legends. Choose a narrative route and complete its stages in order. Either route takes you through the full campaign. Only progress earned after a stage begins counts toward its objectives.

Read examination conditions closely. A clean Tower or Spire examination may require a win within par, no squad knockouts, a pylon disruption, and a response to a signature attack in the same run. Starting the right floor is only part of the task.

Later campaigns require earlier campaigns to be complete. The Master campaign also needs level 70 and a Stage IV Legacy; Grandmaster needs level 100 and Stage V. Any Legacy qualifies once it reaches the required stage. The Hall shows the current requirements and awards a title when you complete a campaign.

title: About Shinobi Journey
tagline: A shared shinobi RPG with solo stories, village life, and player competition, currently in public beta.
blurb: Where to track your progress, get help, adjust the game, and report a problem during public beta.
heroAlt: A wide mountain valley with a distant shinobi village beneath the clouds.
quickTake: Use the Logbook for your next objective and the Living Chronicle to look back over your progress.
Balance and event schedules can change during public beta. Check the current in-game value before spending.
For a bug report, include the screen, the action you took, and what happened. Remove private details from screenshots.

sections.heading: Your progress and the shared world

blocks.text: Shinobi Journey is a persistent browser RPG. You build a shinobi, raise companions, take missions, and travel a shared world. You can follow solo stories, join a clan, or take part in village campaigns.

The Logbook tracks active goals and useful next actions. The Living Chronicle records completed story, mission, exploration, companion, card, war, and Legacy milestones. World Eras and personal Era campaigns are recorded in the Hall of Legends.

The game is open to play while development continues. Systems, rewards, costs, and event schedules may change. These guides were checked in October 2026; if a screen shows a different value, use the current in-game value and report the mismatch.
If a purchase or reward is still unconfirmed, wait for the save to finish. Follow the screen’s recovery instructions before trying again.

sections.heading: How to ask for help or report a bug

blocks.text: Use the Discord link in the game for strategy help and feedback. For build advice, include your level, rank, and the mode you are preparing for. For a bug report, give enough detail for someone else to repeat the problem.

items: Name the screen and the control you used.
Explain what you did just before the problem, what you expected, and what happened.
Include your device and browser. Add a screenshot for a visual problem, with private chat and account details removed.
Keep passwords, sign-in tokens, and private account data out of public reports.

sections.heading: Adjusting the game and giving feedback

blocks.text: Settings lets you choose the Cinematic or Classic story reader, adjust master volume, or mute all audio. These preferences are saved on the device you are using.

When giving feedback, describe the decision or task that felt awkward. A specific example, such as a reward that was hard to find or an unclear entry requirement, helps us understand what needs changing.
